producer_report.summary: The ontology test now compares every term with its governing sources, and file-wide excuses are gone. `claim_problems` in crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs is generic over all terms. It scans BRIEF.md and each term's file sources for lines naming the term or an alias, as a whole word. Each term lists `senses` (source file, whole-word marker, a phrase the definition must say). A stale marker, a missing phrase or a term with no checked claim fails. Every line where a source defines the term or gives it a role (BRIEF.md lines 11, 367, 411, 596, 597) must be covered by a sense. Dropping Hermes's Orchestration sense therefore flags the pantheon row, and restoring it passes. The excuse is optional and bounded: one file, a marker that says more than the term's name, and a reason. It is flagged when stale or when it covers more than two lines. docs/ontology.toml has seven terms with senses and no excuses. Definitions corrected to match their sources: planning (built, turned off by its rule (D135), now for hard jobs only (D143)), Athena (also the third studied instance; the opening of the brief calls the program the system), landed (`merged-unverified` and identified from records), Sri (owns the requirements). D152 in docs/decisions.md and a CHANGELOG bullet record the root cause, the three jobs, the alternatives and why the check lives in the ontology test. The 29 ontology tests, fmt, clippy, the policy scan and the full `cargo test --locked` (exit 0) all pass.

open_issues: The identifying-line rule is a heuristic on line shape. A wrapped continuation line that starts with a term name and a colon, such as `job:` at docs/design/native-pr-landing.md line 148, would need an excuse if that file became a source of the term. It is not a source of `job` today.
MAX_EXCUSED_LINES = 2 is a judgement, not measured. The real file has no excuse, so it bounds only future ones.
docs/records.md still lists the job-plan record as 'not written yet' while docs/design/job-planning.md says planning is built; out of scope for this job and not changed.
mistakes: My first draft of the Sri definition rewrapped 'never he or she' across a line break, which broke the existing seven-term test; fixed by rewrapping.
The first draft of the D152 Case claimed the seeded Hermes entry named only the tool, which is false for the base file; corrected before reporting.
I ran `cargo metadata` with output that was far too large; no effect on the result.
learnings: The base docs/ontology.toml had no senses, aliases or excused fields, and the base test had no claim check, so everything was re-added from base.
Only BRIEF.md lines 11, 367, 411, 596 and 597 start with a term name followed by `:` or `|` for these terms in the scanned files. With senses for each, no excuse is needed.
The phrase `product versus system` appears in no source, so aliases `Loop B` and `first product` give that term its hits (BRIEF.md line 1008).
TOML multi-line definitions wrap lines, so `says` phrases are compared with whitespace collapsed (`flat`); a plain `contains` fails when a phrase falls across a line break.
The Hermes entry in the base file already named both senses; the tool-only case is what the new check would catch, so D152 says 'would have passed' and not that it did.
